newsitem.title: USA: Varian Q1 hurt by soft chip equipment mkt.
newsitem.headline: Varian Q1 hurt by soft chip equipment mkt.

text.p: Varian Associates Inc Thursday reported weaker first-quarter results, as stronger health care systems and instrument sales were offset by soft demand for semiconductor equipment.

It said semiconductor equipment sales of $101 million were off 30 percent from a year before. The ion implant sector caused the decline while thin film products shipments rose modestly. "We are beginning to see some modest improvement in order patterns for this business, suggesting that the down cycle in the equipment market may be at or near its bottom," said chairman and chief executive J. Tracy O'Rourke.
The company reported first-quarter net earnings of $12.8 million or $0.41 per share compared with $25.5 million or $0.79 per share in the year-ago quarter.

As for Varian's semiconductor equipment operations, O'Rourke said because of lower shipments, operating margins for these activities were well below the year-ago level but margins remained in double-digits.
While quarterly comparisons with 1996 will continue to be negative, he said the company is cautiously optimistic that business levels will improve in the second half.

O'Rourke said this business has worked hard to hone its operations and keep costs in line. As a result, he expects it to continue to achieve double-digit operating margins despite the current relatively weak demand picture.
"After achieving record results for three consecutive years, we knew we would have tougher going in fiscal 1997," said O'Rourke. "And in that respect, the first quarter's results were no surprise."
